title: Heat illness
summary: Symptoms after heat or intense exertion. Depending on the combination of symptoms, heat exhaustion, heat cramps or heat stroke (to be ruled out) are considered. Body temperature, if known, comes from an independent source (not from the urine sample). Informational support only: not a diagnosis or a treatment decision. No clinical personnel on board: the steps are first aid and monitoring; treatment depends on mission procedures.

immediate.text: Confusion or collapse with heat exposure: possible heat stroke, emergency.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Call for emergency help and stay with the person.
Move them to a cool place, remove their outer clothing and cool them quickly with cold water, cold wet cloths or ice, and air circulation.
If it is you and you can move: call for help, go to the coolest area and cool yourself with wet cloths and air.

review.text: Heat symptoms with the person conscious: cool down and hydrate.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Get out of the heat, remove extra clothing and cool off with cloths or cold water on your head, face and neck.
If you have cramps: drink water and have a drink or snack with electrolytes every 15 to 20 minutes; avoid salt tablets.
If confusion or loss of consciousness appears, treat it as heat stroke (emergency).

candidates.label: Heat exhaustion
candidates.minimum_evidence: Heat exposure with heavy sweating, dizziness, nausea, headache or feeling unwell.

candidates.label: Heat stroke (must be ruled out)
candidates.minimum_evidence: Heat exposure with confusion, collapse or unresponsiveness.
